People: Henry David Thoreau (author, Wikidata Q131149), died 1862; Ralph Waldo Emerson (other, Wikidata Q48226), died 1882; William Ellery Channing (editor, Wikidata Q2558572), died 1901; Sophia E. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Thoreau, Henry David, 1817-1862; Emerson, Ralph Waldo, 1803-1882 [Contributor]; Channing, William Ellery, 1817-1901 [Editor]; Thoreau, Sophia E., 1819-1876 [Editor]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's (Wikidata gives some of them several death years, every one 1925 or earlier: Sophia E. Thoreau [1871, 1876]).

Printed edition: A yankee in canada with anti-slavery and reform papers, 1878, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/yankeeincanadawi0000henr. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 84%, 94%, 100% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Ralph Waldo Emerson, William Ellery Channing, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
